questions.question: Which of the following statements is true about asthma?
options: It is an infectious disease that spreads through coughing.
It is a non-infectious disease that can cause breathing difficulties.
It is caused by a bacterial pathogen in the lungs.
It is a genetic disease that only affects adults.

questions.question: What physical change occurs in the lungs during an asthma attack?
options: The air sacs (alveoli) fill up with blood.
The breathing (bronchial) tubes narrow.
The diaphragm stops moving up and down.
The ribs fuse together temporarily.

questions.question: Which of these are common symptoms of an asthma attack?
options: Wheezing and shortness of breath
High fever and skin rashes
Uncontrollable sneezing and watery eyes
Sharp chest pain and shivering.

questions.question: How is the medication for treating asthma symptoms typically delivered to the patient?
options: Through a liquid medicine swallowed with water
Through an injection in the arm
Through a device called an inhaler
Through a medicated skin patch

questions.question: Which of the following is considered a risk factor for developing asthma?
options: Eating too much sugar
Having a low birth weight
Experiencing loud noises
Lack of physical exercise

questions.question: What is a defining characteristic of infectious diseases?
options: They are always inherited from parents.
They can be passed from one organism to another.
They are only caused by lifestyle choices.
They cannot be treated with any medicine.

questions.question: What type of organisms or agents are directly responsible for causing infectious diseases?
options: Unbalanced nutrients and minerals
Chemicals from cigarette smoke
Pathogens such as viruses and some bacteria
Genetic mutations in body cells

questions.question: Why can you not catch a non-infectious disease like heart disease from another person?
options: Non-infectious diseases cannot be passed from one organism to another.
Non-infectious diseases are only active during the night.
Non-infectious diseases are killed by the immune system instantly.
Non-infectious diseases only affect plants.

questions.question: How do eating an unbalanced diet and not getting enough exercise affect health?
options: They cause immediate bacterial infections.
They increase the risk of developing lifestyle diseases.
They prevent the transmission of genetic diseases.
They directly cure asthma symptoms.

questions.question: Which set of activities is known to increase the risk of developing lifestyle diseases?
options: Exercising regularly and drinking water
Getting enough sleep and eating vegetables
Smoking, drinking alcohol, and using drugs
Washing hands frequently and avoiding dust

questions.question: Which of the following is a key strategy for preventing lifestyle diseases?
options: Avoiding all vaccinations and medicines
Exercising, eating a balanced diet, and not smoking
Spending more time indoors near air conditioners
Consuming high amounts of caffeine daily

questions.question: What is the main purpose of medicines?
options: They are drugs taken purely for relaxation or fun.
They are drugs that people take when they are ill.
They are substances used to increase athletic speed.
They are chemicals used to clean household surfaces.

questions.question: Recreational drugs can be classified into which two main groups based on their effects on the body?
options: Soluble and insoluble drugs
Natural and synthetic drugs
Depressants and stimulants
Infectious and non-infectious drugs

questions.question: What effect do depressant drugs have on the human body?
options: They speed up heart rate and make you feel energetic.
They slow down thinking and reaction times.
They improve memory retention and eyesight.
They cause instant muscle growth and strength.

questions.question: While alcohol is a legal depressant, what are the risks of long-term alcohol use?
options: It can cause damage to the brain and liver.
It leads to an increase in lung capacity.
It strengthens the bones and joints.
It cures infectious bacterial diseases.

questions.question: What is the primary effect of stimulant drugs on a person?
options: They make you feel drowsy and ready to sleep.
They slow down your reaction times.
They make you feel more alert and can give you quicker thinking and reaction times.
They temporarily block your ability to hear high-pitched sounds.

questions.question: Why is nicotine, found in tobacco leaves, particularly dangerous?
options: It is a highly addictive substance that affects the body.
It causes immediate destruction of the stomach lining.
It cannot be detected in the bloodstream.
It prevents the absorption of water in the large intestine.

questions.question: What is the term used for inhaling common chemicals such as glue or paint thinner to become intoxicated?
options: Solvent abuse
Nicotine vaping
Alcoholic fermentation
Caffeine stimulation

questions.question: Which of the following is a serious risk associated with solvent abuse?
options: Immediate improvement in lung function
Long-term health problems and even death
Immunity to viral infections
Permanent increase in reaction speed

questions.question: Why is vaping considered detrimental to health, similar to smoking cigarettes?
options: It involves consuming carbon dioxide.
It involves consuming nicotine, which is harmful.
It completely stops the heart within minutes.
It causes immediate infectious bacterial diseases.
